# Chunk C4: MCP server and read tools

Paste everything between the two `---` lines into Claude Code, run from your local clone of `ironfis1/cpanel-mail-mcp` with `main` pulled.

---

You are building chunk C4 of cpanel-mail-mcp, a Cloudflare Worker remote MCP server that gives Claude IMAP access to Scott's three cPanel business mailboxes. Read `docs/spec.md` (tag `spec-v1.3`), `docs/build/traceability.md`, `docs/prerequisites.md` and `docs/build/spec-questions.md` before writing code.

## Goal

Stand up the MCP server (streamable HTTP) on staging and implement the read tools: accounts, availability, folders, emails, search, thread, with per-account failure handling.

## Rules for this chunk (read first)

1. Build to `docs/spec.md` at git tag `spec-v1.3`. Do not edit `docs/spec.md`, `docs/rule-base.md`, `docs/ambiguity-log.md` or `docs/design.md`.
2. Implement only the requirements listed under "In scope". Do not add behavior the spec does not state, even if it seems obviously useful.
3. If a requirement is unclear, contradicts another, or needs a decision the spec does not make: do not decide it. Add an entry to `docs/build/spec-questions.md` (format below), skip that item, finish the rest, and list the question in the PR. Scott resolves it and, if needed, the spec gets a version bump.
4. Every automated test's name starts with the REQ IDs it verifies, for example `REQ-4-7 REQ-4-8: greeting times out after 5 s`.
5. Add `node scripts/trace.mjs --chunk C4 --strict` to the unit job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, next to the earlier chunks' lines.
5a. Fill the "Verified by" column of `docs/build/traceability.md` for every in-scope row (test file and test name, or the manual check to perform). Set Status to `built` for automated rows that pass, or `needs Scott` for manual rows.
6. No secrets in the repo, logs, test output or PR. Passwords are entered by Scott with `wrangler secret put` only. Never print a secret value.
7. Work on branch `chunk/C4`. Open a pull request titled `C4: MCP server and read tools`. Do not merge it. Stop after opening the PR.
8. The PR description contains: in-scope REQs and their status, the exact commands you ran with their pass/fail results, anything deferred and why, and any spec questions raised.

Spec question format (append to `docs/build/spec-questions.md`):

```
## Q<n> (C4)
REQ: <id(s)>
Question: <what is unclear>
Options: <2 or 3 readings>
Blocking: <yes/no; what is skipped until answered>
Resolution:
```

## Deliverables

- MCP server endpoint on the staging Worker, protected by the temporary `STAGING_TOKEN` bearer (replaced by OAuth in C6).
- Tools `accounts`, `availability`, `folders`, `emails`, `search`, `thread` with input schemas matching the Spark schemas recorded in `docs/proposed-resolutions.md` (REQ-18-3) and the output fields in REQ-18-4.
- Sessions and concurrency per section 4.3, using the C1 client.
- Per-account failure reporting and the error set in REQ-12-11.

## Required tests

- Unit tests per tool against the fake server.
- Integration (staging) for each tool on both test mailboxes, including a forced failure (bad host for one account) to prove the other account still returns results (REQ-12-1, REQ-12-2).

- From the C2 review: message IDs are base64 JSON, not signed, so a caller can hand in any account and folder. Every tool that takes an ID must check the decoded account against the registry (REQ-6-3) before any IMAP call. REQ-2-19 is partial after C2: add the tool-layer test to its "Verified by" cell.

## Success criteria (all must hold before the PR is ready)

- All in-scope rows filled and passing.
- Integration job green.
- `node scripts/trace.mjs --chunk C4 --strict` passes.
- No new spec questions left unlisted in the PR.
